articles.title: How PlumbobForge works
articles.summary: Your CC lives in the Library, sorted into sets. A configuration decides which sets the game loads.
questions: How does this app work?
Where do I start?
What is a set?
What is a configuration?
steps: Add your CC in the **Library** tab. Each file becomes an item.
Group items into **sets**, like folders: by creator, style, or type.
In **Configurations**, choose which sets the game should load. The active configuration is what you play with.
In Library mode, click the **Rebuild** button in the title bar to send your changes to the game. In Vault mode, changes apply on their own.
tips: Press **Ctrl+K** to jump to any set, item or configuration by name.

articles.title: Add CC to your library
articles.summary: Drop your downloaded files onto the Library and they're imported into the selected set.
questions: How do I add CC?
How do I install mods?
Can I import a zip file?
Where do my downloads go?
steps: Open the **Library** tab.
Select the set you want the new items in. If you skip this, pick a set later with **Move to Set**.
Drag your files from File Explorer onto the item grid. **.package**, **.sims3pack**, **.zip**, **.7z** and **.rar** all work, and archives are unpacked for you.
If some files are already in your library, choose whether to **Rename (Keep Both)**, **Replace Existing** or **Skip Duplicates**.
tips: Archives can hold many packages. Each one becomes its own item.

articles.title: Import new CC automatically
articles.summary: Let PlumbobForge watch a folder, like your Downloads, and import new packages from it.
questions: Can it import my downloads automatically?
How do I watch a folder?
steps: Go to **Settings** → **Monitored Folders & Auto-Import**.
Click **Add Folder** and pick the folder you download CC into.
Turn on **Auto-Import on Launch** to check it every time PlumbobForge starts.
Or click **Scan & Import Now** to import right away.

articles.title: Move over from CC Magic or Sims 3 Mod Organizer
articles.summary: Bring your packages, sets and configurations over from another CC manager.
questions: I used CC Magic before
How do I import from S3MO?
Can I keep my old sets?
steps: Go to **Settings** → **Maintenance & Diagnostics** and click **Open Migration Tool**.
Pick **CC Magic** or **Sims 3 Mod Organizer** and check the installation folder.
Choose **Full Migration** to bring over sets and configurations too, or **Simple Migration** to only move the packages.
Click **Start Migration** and wait for it to finish.

articles.title: Get your changes into the game
articles.summary: In Library mode, the game only sees your changes after a rebuild.
questions: My changes don't show in the game
What does the orange button mean?
How do I apply changes?
steps: When something changes, the **Rebuild** button in the title bar (the circular arrows) turns orange.
Close The Sims 3. The game keeps the cache files open, so a rebuild can't run while it's open.
Click the **Rebuild** button and wait for it to finish.
If things still look wrong, right-click the button and choose **Force Rebuild** to rebuild everything from scratch.
tips: In Vault mode there's nothing to rebuild: the title bar shows the vault status instead.

articles.title: Jump anywhere with Quick Jump
articles.summary: Find any set, item, configuration or page by typing its name.
questions: Is there a keyboard shortcut to search?
How do I find a set quickly?
steps: Press **Ctrl+K**, or click **Quick Jump** in the title bar.
Start typing a name.
Use the arrow keys and press **Enter**, or click a result to go there.

articles.title: Create a set or sub-set
articles.summary: Sets work like folders for your CC. You can nest them too.
questions: How do I make a new set?
Can I put a set inside another set?
How do I make folders?
steps: In the **Library**, click the **+** button at the top of the sets sidebar on the left (**New Set**).
Type a name and confirm.
To nest a set, right-click an existing set and choose **Add Sub-Set**.
tips: Turning off a set in a configuration also turns off its sub-sets.

articles.title: Give a set an icon and color
articles.summary: Make sets easier to tell apart in the sidebar.
questions: How do I change a set's color?
Can I rename a set?
How do I sort my sets?
How do I rename a folder?
steps: Right-click a set in the sidebar and choose **Customize Set**.
Click the avatar to pick an icon, then choose a color.
Rename it at the top and click **Save Changes**.
To change the order, use the sort button at the top of the sidebar (name, recently added, or item count).

articles.title: Move items to another set
articles.summary: Drag items onto a set, or use Move to Set.
questions: How do I move CC between sets?
How do I put items in a set?
How do I move files into a folder?
steps: Select the items (see **Select several items at once**).
Drag them onto a set in the sidebar.
Or click **Move to Set** in the toolbar above the items and pick the set.
tips: Moving a set onto a set with the same name lets you merge them or rename the one you're moving.

articles.title: Delete a set
articles.summary: Remove a set and choose what happens to the items inside.
questions: How do I delete a set without losing the CC?
How do I remove a folder?
How do I delete a folder without deleting my CC?
steps: Right-click the set and choose **Delete**.
Pick **Keep items and move them to Default set**, or delete the packages along with it.
Click **Delete Set**. Any sub-sets move up to the top level.

articles.title: Select several items at once
articles.summary: Most actions work on everything you've selected.
questions: How do I select more than one item?
Can I edit many items at once?
steps: Click an item to select it.
Hold **Ctrl** and click to add or remove items, or hold **Shift** to select a range.
Drag a box around items in empty space to select them all.
Use **Select All** in the toolbar to select everything shown.
tips: Right-click your selection to see what you can do with it.

articles.title: Turn items on or off
articles.summary: Turned-off items stay in your library but the game doesn't load them.
questions: How do I disable a mod without deleting it?
How do I turn off CC?
steps: Select the items.
Click **Toggle Selected** in the toolbar, or right-click and choose it.
In Library mode, **Rebuild** to apply it in the game.
tips: To turn off just one object inside a package, use **Look Inside**.
To turn items on or off for one configuration only, use **Include** and **Exclude** in Configurations.

articles.title: Mark favorites
articles.summary: Star the items you love so they're easy to find.
questions: How do I favorite an item?
Where are my favorites?
steps: Hover an item and click the **star**, or select several and click **Favorite Selected** in the toolbar.
Open **Favorites** in the sets sidebar to see them all.
In the **Sort** menu, **Favorites First** keeps them at the top of every set.

articles.title: Delete items
articles.summary: Remove CC from your library for good.
questions: How do I delete CC?
How do I uninstall a mod?
steps: Select the items.
Click **Delete Selected** in the toolbar, or right-click and delete.
Confirm. Files go to the Recycle Bin unless you tick the box to delete them permanently.
tips: Not sure? Turn the items off instead. You can always turn them back on.

articles.title: Change how items are shown
articles.summary: Switch between a grid and a compact list, resize thumbnails and sort.
questions: How do I make the thumbnails bigger?
Can I see items as a list?
steps: Use the view buttons in the toolbar to switch between **Grid View** and **Compact List View**.
Drag the **Thumbnail Zoom** slider to resize the cards.
Open **Sort** to order by name or recently added.

articles.title: Keyboard shortcuts
articles.summary: Work through your library without the mouse: open, switch on or off, favorite and find items with a key.
questions: Are there keyboard shortcuts?
How do I select all items?
How do I rename a set quickly?
steps: Click an item first, so the keys go to the item list.
**Enter** opens the selected items with **Look Inside**.
**Space** switches the selected items on or off.
**F** adds them to Favorites, or takes them out.
**Delete** deletes them, after asking.
**Ctrl+A** selects every item in the list, and **Ctrl+F** jumps to the search box.
In the sidebar, **Up** and **Down** move between sets, **Right** and **Left** open and close a set with subsets, and **F2** renames the selected set.
tips: The keys are also shown next to their entries when you right-click an item.
Keys do nothing while you're typing in a box.

articles.title: Find items with filters
articles.summary: Narrow the library down by type, category, age, room and more.
questions: How do I find all hairs?
How do I see only build mode items?
How do I search my CC?
Show only teen clothes
steps: Open the **Filters** sidebar on the right of the Library.
Type in the search box to search names and tags.
Pick a type (**CAS Items**, **Build / Buy** or **Other Content**) to see the filters for it, like CAS category, age, gender, room or function.
Click **Clear All** to start over.
tips: Filters work together, so Hair + Teen + Female shows only teen female hair.

articles.title: Fix an item's category or tags
articles.summary: If something is sorted under the wrong category, age or room, you can correct it with Edit Tags & Categories.
questions: My hair is under the wrong category
This item shows up in the wrong place
The age or gender is wrong
How do I change an item's category?
steps: Select the item, or several at once.
Right-click and choose **Edit Tags & Categories**, or click the tag button on the item card.
Fix the category, age group, gender or outfit category. For Build/Buy items, set the room and function.
Click **Apply Changes**.
tips: This changes how PlumbobForge sorts and filters the item. It doesn't change the package file itself.
When you run **Recheck Package Types**, keep **Skip packages that have manual user tags** ticked so your fixes stay.

articles.title: Use your own tags
articles.summary: Tag items with anything you like, such as a creator, style or era, and filter by it.
questions: Can I tag items by creator?
How do I add my own tags?
How do I filter by tag?
steps: Select items, right-click and choose **Edit Tags & Categories**.
Type tags in **Custom User Tags**, separated by commas (for example: Simsimi, Victorian).
Click **Apply Changes**.
Find them later by typing the tag in the **Filters** search box.

articles.title: Look inside an item
articles.summary: See every CAS part, object and thumbnail a package contains.
questions: What's inside this package?
How do I see the objects in a file?
steps: Select one or more items.
Right-click and choose **Look Inside**.
Pick an object on the left to see its details and thumbnails.
With several items selected, switch between them at the top, or look at all of them together.

articles.title: Turn single objects off
articles.summary: Keep one object or CAS part out of the game without disabling the whole package.
questions: I only want one item from this set
How do I hide one object from a package?
How do I stop townies wearing this?
steps: Open the item with **Look Inside**.
Select the object and switch off **In game**. Use **Turn all off** for every object at once.
For CAS parts, switch off **Valid for random** to stop the game putting them on townies and newborns.
Close The Sims 3, save your changes, then **Rebuild** in Library mode.
tips: The package file isn't changed. Turned-off Build/Buy objects disappear from lots they were placed on.

articles.title: Change or export thumbnails
articles.summary: Replace, remove, add or save the thumbnails inside a package.
questions: How do I change a thumbnail?
Can I save the preview images?
The thumbnail is ugly
steps: Open the item with **Look Inside** and pick an object.
Use **Replace...**, **Remove** or **Add thumbnails...** under its thumbnails. PNG, JPG, BMP, WebP and GIF all work.
Use **Export...** to save them as images.
Close The Sims 3 and save your changes.
tips: Still seeing the old thumbnail in game? Clear the **Thumbnails Cache** in Tools → Cache Cleaner.

articles.title: See how many triangles an item has
articles.summary: Look Inside counts the triangles of CAS parts and Build/Buy objects, so you can spot the ones that slow the game down.
questions: How many polygons does this item have?
Which CC makes my game lag?
How do I find high-poly CC?
steps: Open the item with **Look Inside**. Every object shows its triangle count in the list, and a **Heavy** tag when it is large.
Pick an object to see its **Mesh size** card: triangles, vertices and every detail level.
Click **3D** on its thumbnail to look at the mesh itself, with its textures and every detail level.
Click **Heaviest first** to sort by size, or **heavy** to show only the heavy ones.
On **All items**, switch off the heaviest objects with their toggles.
tips: Triangles are counted from the most detailed level. Heavy is a rough guide, not a limit.
Items that use the game's own mesh are shown as such, because there is nothing to count.
To check the whole library at once, use Tools → Mesh Report.

articles.title: Create a configuration
articles.summary: A configuration is a list of sets for the game to load: one per save, playstyle or test.
questions: How do I make a new config?
Can I have different CC for different saves?
How do I copy a configuration?
steps: Open the **Configurations** tab.
Click the **+** button at the top of the list (**New Configuration**).
Choose which sets it loads (see **Choose which sets a configuration loads**).
To start from an existing one, right-click it and choose **Duplicate Configuration**.

articles.title: Switch to another configuration
articles.summary: The active configuration is what the game loads.
questions: How do I change which config the game uses?
How do I switch configurations?
steps: Close The Sims 3.
In **Configurations**, right-click the configuration and choose **Set as Active**.
Wait for it to apply. The active one has an **ACTIVE** badge.

articles.title: Choose which sets a configuration loads
articles.summary: Move sets between Enabled Sets and Disabled Sets.
questions: How do I turn off a set for one save?
How do I enable a set in a configuration?
steps: Select the configuration in **Configurations**.
Drag sets between **Enabled Sets** and **Disabled Sets**.
Or select sets and use the arrow buttons between the lists (**Swap Sets**).
Use the search box above each list to find a set by name.
tips: Disabling a set also disables its sub-sets.

articles.title: Include or exclude single items
articles.summary: Load one item from a disabled set, or leave one out of an enabled set, in this configuration only.
questions: I want one item from a set I've disabled
How do I leave out one item from a set?
steps: Select the configuration.
Click **Include** above Enabled Sets to pick items to load even though their set is disabled.
Click **Exclude** above Disabled Sets to pick items to leave out even though their set is enabled.
To undo, remove the item from the list and it follows its set again.
tips: Turn on **Items First** to see these items above the sets.

articles.title: Rename or customize a configuration
articles.summary: Give a configuration a name, description, icon and color.
questions: How do I rename a config?
How do I delete a configuration?
steps: Right-click the configuration and choose **Customize Configuration**.
Change the name and description, click the avatar to pick an icon, and choose a color.
Click **Save Changes**.
To remove a configuration, right-click it and choose **Delete Configuration**.

articles.title: Clean the game's caches
articles.summary: Clearing The Sims 3's cache files fixes many odd problems and old thumbnails.
questions: How do I clear the cache?
Which cache files should I delete?
Old CC still shows up
steps: Close The Sims 3.
Go to **Tools** → **Cache Cleaner**.
Click **Select Recommended**, or tick the caches you want.
Click **Clean Selected Caches**.
tips: Each cache explains when and why to clear it.
To do this automatically after every change, turn on **Clear game caches after changes** in Settings → In-Game Performance.

articles.title: Fix the 'Materializing Materials' stall
articles.summary: Broken custom patterns can make Create-a-Style hang. Pattern Fixer finds and repairs them.
questions: Create a Style is stuck on Materializing Materials
My patterns are broken
CASt freezes
steps: Go to **Tools** → **Pattern Fixer**.
Click **Scan Patterns**.
Click **Fix All Broken**, or select patterns and click **Fix Selected Patterns**.

articles.title: Create a Build/Buy collection
articles.summary: Turn your sets into in-game catalog collections with their own icon.
questions: How do I make a collection?
Can I find my CC in one place in buy mode?
How do I hide CC from the catalog?
steps: Go to **Tools** → **Collection Creator** and click **New Collection**.
Name it and pick an **In-Game Icon**, or use **Import PNG...** for your own.
Under **Add CC Sets**, click **+ Add** on the sets you want. Use **Include Items** to add single Build/Buy items without their whole set.
Save. Turn on **Hide objects in catalog** to show them only in this collection.
tips: Collections made outside PlumbobForge show up too. Saving one turns it into a PlumbobForge collection.

articles.title: Find duplicate and conflicting CC
articles.summary: Conflict Scanner finds duplicate files, mods that override each other and damaged packages.
questions: Do I have duplicate CC?
Which mods conflict?
How do I find broken packages?
steps: Go to **Tools** → **Conflict Scanner** and click **Scan for Conflicts**.
Filter by **Duplicate Files**, **Resource Overrides**, **Incompatibilities** or **Corrupt Packages**.
Use **Disable Redundant Duplicates** to fix all duplicates in one click, or **Keep Only This** on a single group.
Use **Ignore Conflict** for overrides you want, such as a mod meant to replace another.

articles.title: Find high-poly items in your whole library
articles.summary: Mesh Report counts the triangles of every CAS part and object and lists the heaviest first.
questions: Which of my CC is the heaviest?
How do I make my game run faster?
Can I see poly counts for everything?
steps: Go to **Tools** → **Mesh Report** and click **Count triangles**.
The list shows the **Heavy** items first. Choose **All** to see everything, or filter by CAS and Build / Buy.
Use **Open in CC Optimizer** to make heavy items lighter, **Look Inside** to switch an item off, or **View in Library** to remove it.
tips: Nothing is changed by the scan itself.
Heavy is a rough guide: one heavy item matters less than hundreds of medium ones.

articles.title: Make heavy CC lighter
articles.summary: The CC Optimizer lowers the triangle count of hair, clothes, accessories and build/buy objects while keeping their shape, and shows the result in 3D before you save.
questions: How do I lower the poly count of my CC?
Can I make high-poly hair lighter?
How do I reduce triangles?
Can I optimize all my heavy CC at once?
steps: Open **Tools** → **CC Optimizer** and click **+** next to **Items**, or in **Mesh Report** click **Open in CC Optimizer** to send every very heavy item (the arrow next to it adds the heavy ones too).
Pick an item in the list and choose how many triangles to keep. Every item starts at 50%.
Switch between **Before** and **After** over the model and turn it with the mouse to check it still looks right.
Click **Save** to save every item in the list. Library items go to the Recycle Bin first, so you can get the old file back.
tips: **Advanced** has the detail levels (close-up, mid distance, far away), **Simplify distance versions automatically** and **Keep seams closed**. Each setting says when it's recommended. If one isn't, a note under the slider says so, and **Reset to recommended** puts them back. **Use these settings for all items** copies the selected item's settings to the rest.

The bar under the preview switches between plain and in-game textures, picks a colour, shows the triangles and, under **Other**, the separate images a texture is made from. It only changes the preview, not the saved file.
Items you haven't opened are saved at their starting amount, so check the ones you care about first.
Hair keeps its inner layer: it is rebuilt from the reduced outer layer.
An object is listed once with all of its colour variants, since they share the same meshes. Shadows are left as they are, and recolourable objects show without their texture.
Optimizing can be undone. The original meshes are kept: open the item in the CC Optimizer again to see where its sliders stand and move them back to 100%, or use **Undo optimization** in Look Inside.
Look Inside can send one part, or all of an item's parts, to the CC Optimizer too.

articles.title: Pin a tool as a tab
articles.summary: Put the tools you use most right in the title bar.
questions: Can I add a tool to the top bar?
steps: Open **Tools** and open the tool list at the top.
Click the pin next to a tool (**Pin as a tab**).
Click it again to unpin.

articles.title: Change the theme and accent color
articles.summary: Dark, light or system theme, any accent color, or a theme built from your own color.
questions: How do I turn on dark mode?
Can I change the colors?
How do I make it pink?
steps: Go to **Settings** → **Appearance & Personalization**.
Pick a **Theme Mode**: Dark, Light or System.
Pick an **Accent Color** for buttons and highlights.
For your own palette, choose the **Custom Theme Generator**, enter a base color and adjust **Tint Strength**.

articles.title: Change the language
articles.summary: PlumbobForge is available in English and Polish.
questions: How do I change the language?
steps: Go to **Settings** → **Appearance & Personalization**.
Pick a **Language**. It changes right away.

articles.title: Library mode or Vault mode?
articles.summary: Library mode keeps your original files and builds a cache. Vault mode stores everything once and needs no rebuilds.
questions: What is Vault mode?
How do I save disk space?
How do I go back to Library mode?
steps: Go to **Settings** → **Storage Mode**.
**Library Mode** keeps your originals plus a cache for the game. It's stable and the default.
**Vault Mode** keeps one copy (about half the disk space) and switches configurations in seconds. It's still experimental.
Click **Switch to Vault Mode** and choose a backup option, or **Revert to Library Mode** to go back.
tips: In Vault mode, **Clean Up Wasted Disk Space** frees space from CC you've deleted or updated.

articles.title: Dynamic Cache or Static Bundle?
articles.summary: Choose how Library mode builds the files the game loads.
questions: What's the difference between dynamic and static?
Which cache mode is faster?
steps: Go to **Settings** → **Storage Mode** → **Cache Generation Mode**.
**Dynamic Cache** builds one cache per set: quick rebuilds and quick configuration changes.
**Static Bundle** merges all active sets into one bundle for faster loading in game, but every change needs a full rebuild.
With Static Bundle, **Auto-Rebuild Static Cache** rebuilds right after each change. Turn it off to make several changes first.

articles.title: Recheck package types
articles.summary: Reads every package again to refresh its type, CAS category, ages and genders.
questions: Lots of items have the wrong type
How do I re-detect categories?
steps: Go to **Settings** → **Maintenance & Diagnostics**.
Click **Recheck Package Types**.
Keep **Skip packages that have manual user tags/overrides** ticked to keep the fixes you made yourself.
Click **Start Scan**.

articles.title: Run the Auto-Fix routine
articles.summary: Repairs common problems in PlumbobForge's database and rebuilds everything.
questions: Something is broken in my library
Items have no set
steps: Close The Sims 3.
Go to **Settings** → **Maintenance & Diagnostics**.
Click **Run Auto-Fix Routine**. Items without a set move to Default, and every set is rebuilt.

articles.title: Set your game folders
articles.summary: Tell PlumbobForge where The Sims 3 and your user folder are.
questions: PlumbobForge can't find my game
Where is my Sims 3 folder set?
I moved my game
steps: Go to **Settings** → **Storage & Paths**.
Check **The Sims 3 Directory** (where the game is installed).
Check **The Sims 3 User Documents Folder** (in Documents\Electronic Arts). Leave it empty to detect it automatically.
Use **Browse...** to change one, or **Auto-Detect** to find it again.

articles.title: Move your library to another drive
articles.summary: Store your CC somewhere with more space.
questions: My C drive is full
How do I move my CC to another drive?
steps: Go to **Settings** → **Storage & Paths**.
Next to **PlumbobForge Library Directory**, click **Browse...** and pick the new folder.
Choose **Move all files from current library to new path**, then **Confirm**.

articles.title: My CC doesn't show up in the game
articles.summary: Go through these checks one by one.
questions: My CC doesn't show in game
I can't find my hair in CAS
The mod isn't working
Items are missing in buy mode
steps: Check the item is turned on in the Library, and that no object is turned off in **Look Inside**.
Check its set is under **Enabled Sets** in the active configuration.
In Library mode, close the game and click **Rebuild** if the button is orange.
Check your game folders in **Settings** → **Storage & Paths**.
Clean the caches with **Tools** → **Cache Cleaner**.
tips: Sims3Pack files may need the matching expansion or store content to show up.

articles.title: The game crashes or won't load
articles.summary: Find what's causing it and narrow it down.
questions: My game crashes on load
The game freezes
Sims 3 won't start after adding CC
steps: Run **Tools** → **Conflict Scanner** and fix any **Corrupt Packages** and duplicates.
Clean the caches with **Tools** → **Cache Cleaner**.
Duplicate your configuration, disable the sets you added most recently, and test again to narrow it down.
Still crashing? Send a bug report with the bug button in the title bar and tick the Sims 3 logs.

articles.title: The game is slow or takes long to load
articles.summary: A few settings and tools can speed things up.
questions: The game takes forever to load
My game lags with CC
steps: Remove duplicates with **Disable Redundant Duplicates** in the Conflict Scanner.
Try **Static Bundle** in **Settings** → **Storage Mode** for faster loading.
Turn on **Clear game caches after changes** in **Settings** → **In-Game Performance**.
Load fewer sets: make a lighter configuration with only what that save needs.

articles.title: The game shows old or wrong thumbnails
articles.summary: The game keeps its own copies of thumbnails.
questions: The thumbnail in game is wrong
Thumbnails didn't update
steps: Close The Sims 3.
Go to **Tools** → **Cache Cleaner**, tick **Thumbnails Cache** and click **Clean Selected Caches**.

articles.title: A rebuild fails or skips files
articles.summary: What to do when the rebuild stops or reports skipped packages.
questions: Rebuild says the game is running
Some files were skipped
The rebuild failed
steps: Make sure The Sims 3 is fully closed, then try again.
Skipped files are usually damaged or incomplete downloads. Download them again or delete them.
Try **Force Rebuild** (right-click the Rebuild button).
Still failing? Run **Auto-Fix** in **Settings** → **Maintenance & Diagnostics**.

articles.title: Report a bug or ask a question
articles.summary: Send feedback straight from the app, with your logs if you want.
questions: How do I report a bug?
Who do I contact?
I have an idea for a feature
steps: Click the **bug button** in the title bar.
Pick what it's about and describe what happened.
Leave your Tumblr username or email if you'd like a reply.
Keep the logs ticked for bugs. Your Windows username is removed from them.
